basis: The DG COMP merger case register is Commission-owned content released as open data: the Commission's legal notice states its reuse policy ('Unless otherwise indicated (e.g. in individual copyright notices), content owned by the EU on this website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence'), read 2026-10-24 at https://ec.europa.eu/info/legal-notice_en, and DG COMP's own release announcement states the machine-readable case data sets are released under the Commission reuse notice 'so that the machine-readable data sets can be processed in any way the users may wish, for commercial or non-commercial purposes, provided that the source is acknowledged' (https://competition-policy.ec.europa.eu/about/news/dg-competitions-case-data-available-open-data-2025-03-18_en, read 2026-10-24). CC BY 4.0 permits sharing and adapting for any purpose, commercially, provided attribution is given and changes are indicated, so the standing defaults apply: our code and documentation are MIT, our rights in the derived compilation are dedicated CC0-1.0, and the source's own terms are preserved, never relicensed.

third_party.terms: MIT - the harness benchmark's own runner files, shipped verbatim and unmodified (bundled sha256 equal the benchmark's declared hashes, recorded in the baseline job result)
third_party.permission: The benchmark checkout is read-only; permission to distribute verbatim copies of its runner files covers the distributed copies only

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the notified-case eligibility frame, the derived Phase II opener label, the notification-date feature derivations, the temporal partition, and the packaging - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying merger case register keeps its own designation and remains subject to the Commission's CC BY 4.0 reuse terms, whose attribution condition carries through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source.status: European Commission reuse policy, CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise indicated: applies to Commission-owned content, and DG COMP explicitly released the machine-readable merger case data sets under that reuse notice for commercial and non-commercial processing with acknowledgement of the source. Reuse is allowed provided appropriate credit is given and changes are indicated. The dataset's derived rows are indicated changes: a row selection, a derived binary label and derived features, not the Commission's own product.
evidence: [https://competition-policy.ec.europa.eu/about/news/dg-competitions-case-data-available-open-data-2025-03-18_en, read 2026-10-24] 'We are releasing the data under the European Commission reuse notice, so that the machine-readable data sets can be processed in any way the users may wish, for commercial or non-commercial purposes, provided that the source is acknowledged.'

[https://ec.europa.eu/info/legal-notice_en, read 2026-10-24] 'The European Commission's reuse policy is implemented by the Commission Decision of 12 December 2011 on the reuse of Commission documents. Unless otherwise indicated (e.g. in individual copyright notices), content owned by the EU on this website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence. This means that reuse is allowed, provided that appropriate credit is given and changes are indicated.'

Contains Commission-owned content licensed under CC BY 4.0.
source.citation: European Commission, Directorate-General for Competition. EU Competition: Merger case publications (machine-readable case register, open data). https://competition-cases.ec.europa.eu/ . Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (Commission reuse notice). Derived dataset: EU merger Phase II opening prediction task (not a Commission official product).
source.derived_labelling: Labelled as a derived research dataset throughout; it is not the European Commission's official product and the Commission has not reviewed or endorsed it. The publisher's own designation, attribution and suggested citation are preserved verbatim, and changes from the source are indicated (row selection, derived label, derived features).

conditions: Attribution to the European Commission (DG COMP merger case register) as the source, with the CC BY 4.0 licence named, in every copy of the data.
Changes are indicated: the dataset ships a row selection, a derived binary label and derived features, and is labelled as derived, never as the Commission's official product.
Our contribution is dedicated CC0-1.0; the source's CC BY 4.0 terms are preserved and carry through unchanged.
Our code and documentation are MIT.

operator_acceptance.note: No operator acceptance is needed or recorded: the source states terms (Commission reuse notice, CC BY 4.0) that permit redistribution with attribution and indication of changes, and this release stays within them.
